system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the fourth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 3 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

A. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 2

B. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 rectangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 3

C. Draw 2 straight lines on this rectangle to divide it into 1 rectangle and 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

Answer each of the 3 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

answer_3.description: Your answer to question 3, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_3.title: Answer 3

output.answer_1: Draw one straight diagonal line from one corner of the rectangle to the opposite corner (for example, from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner). This divides the rectangle into 2 triangles.
output.answer_2: Draw one straight line from the midpoint of the top side straight down to the midpoint of the bottom side (a vertical line parallel to the left and right sides). This divides the rectangle into 2 smaller rectangles.
output.answer_3: Draw one straight diagonal line from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner, and draw a second straight line from the top-right corner to the bottom-left corner only partway, so that the two lines form a triangle at one end. Concretely: draw a vertical line from the top side down to the bottom side near the right end, and draw a diagonal line from the top-left corner down to the bottom side at that vertical line's bottom point, so the figure splits into 1 rectangle on the left and 2 triangles on the right.
